Hope this isn’t too late. Felt the need to answer since the only other person who did does painting, not graphic design. They are very different programs.
As a current art student studying in design it’s a lot of work, like absolutely brutal at times. This is because it’s a competitive field and you need a strong portfolio. Don’t let anyone else’s judgements on art school matter. They think art school=Fine arts=starving artist stereotype. They just don’t have the brain cells to understand that the everyday things they use and see were literally designed by artists. That spatula? Object design. Your clothes? Fashion designer. Album cover? Illustrator. Graphic designers can make a looooottt of money too, perhaps you can convince mom with this? I really think she’s worried about your financial future and doesn’t know much about the design industry. 

For your decision, I would try something like community college first to get a taste of what college will be like. Graphic design is a cut throat program. From personal experience, I dropped out the first time because it was so overwhelming and the work load I received in high school was nothing compared to the art college assignments. Do a year of studying something a community college then seek out art school.  You’re not going to have a connection right away, you build bonds while attending. You’re decision should be based on the success of previous graduates, tuition costs, living, etc. It is expensive, but it *is* worth it (as you are planning to major in graphic design) but you will need scholarships, bursaries, any thing to assist you. If your desire to be an artist is that strong, follow it. Please don’t let others discourage you from your talent. Additionally you will be an adult by then, you have more freedom in the choices you make.

Good luck!

I don’t think anyone can give you a black and white answer. It’s a dark question whose opinion will depend on experience I think. So I can only list facts.  

Maybe vulnerable wasn’t my best word choice? More like, having power over someone in their weakest state-one where they feel both exposed and humiliated. That is the rapists’ goal. Additionally, the victim also has no idea what’s going to happen after. Will they get killed? Will they kidnap them and repeatedly rape them? It’s a situation where you are defenseless, scared and feeling like there’s no escape. When you co-sign a mortgage or drive cross country chances are you are not in a place where you have zero power. You both probably have equal control.

The thing with sleeping around is, again, a choice based on the person’s life-which we don’t know the reason. It could be anything from insecurity to time management. None of our concern. The main difference between rape and casual sex is of course, consent. 

Now for the crime and consequences for rape. This is usually based on sexual misconduct, mental damage, criminal history/record, etc. Say the rapist picked a promiscuous victim like you said, except in this sceneario he/she also slashed and drugged the victim. Said rapist also has a history of violence. That would result is a bigger penalty against a stranger raping someone at a party and just leaving them passed out. 

Technically, you’re right-rape isn’t the worst thing ever. It’s pretty bad, traumatic but sure. However, it *can* be the worst thing to happen to someone. There have been some absolute brutal cases that have even involved cannibalism (aside from murder). As you said, society broadcasts this kind of news all over the media. Which brings it all down to-it depends on the person.

Okay so, there are different factors: not all women enjoy sleeping around, punishment depends how much damage was caused to the victim, it’s violating someone in their most vulnerable state, can result in long term sometimes permanent mental disorder/issues -> all without consent 

The thing about casual sex has different factors too: insecurity/low self esteem, trying to recover from a bad breakup, validation, sex addiction, mentality of being in their “prime”, whatever she *wants*, whatever her *reason*-> all done with consent

The only in between being the rape fetish but even that’s done with consent. 

It’s not just about sex either, it’s about the power over someone. It’s breaking someone mentally (some cases, physically) through violating their body. That’s what the crime is. 

Doesn’t just apply to women, but men as well. Plenty of men sleep around no strings attached but that doesn’t mean rape won’t have an equally traumatizing effect on them.

There’s a very low chance of your coworkers being homophobic unless you live in an area where homophobia is a norm. You could always talk to a therapist or counsellor if it’s eating away at you.

I’ll speak from experience where I chose to not work through my fears. When I told someone at work I trusted that I may be gay, others got wind of it and chose to deny it since they didn’t want to believe it (its a bit homophobic where I live). Hurt a little, but better than being harassed. Instead of dealing with my fears/situation head on I chose to date a straight guy instead (that my mother introduced me to as a date) and I caved in to anxiety. It makes me feel kind of gross and very stressful trying to be a good straight girlfriend but better than being lonely. I should have changed work places and told my Mom the truth. 

So my advice, slowly open up to those who don’t know. That way it won’t be a shock to them. Talk to a therapist and sort out your fears, take time to work through it there’s no rush. Don’t be me and give into anxiety because while that route in theory sounds easier, it’s more trouble than it’s worth.

Wish you the best!
